# Aviation Archaeology

> > AAIR provides comprehensive aviation archaeology research, crash site investigation services, and searchable accident report databases for military and civil aircraft.

Aviation Archaeological Investigation & Research (AAIR) is a specialized organization dedicated to documenting, preserving, and researching aircraft crash sites and aviation history. The site offers searchable databases of USAF, Navy, civil aviation, and Vietnam War-era aircraft losses, along with technical reference materials and field investigation services.

## Key Topics

- Aviation archaeology
- Crash site documentation
- Aircraft accident reports
- USAF military records
- Historic preservation
- Aircraft identification
- Military aviation
- Searchable databases
- Aircraft part numbers
- Field investigation
- AAIR (Aviation Archaeological Investigation & Research)
- Vietnam War aircraft losses
- Aircraft manufacturer prefixes
- Inspection stamps
- Expedition research

## Accident Report Databases

- [Select USAF Database](https://aviationarchaeology.com/dbSelectAirForce.asp): Searchable USAF accident reports and MACR records database
- [Select Civil Database](https://aviationarchaeology.com/dbSelectCivil.asp): Searchable U.S. civil aviation accident reports 1933-2008
- [Select USN Database](https://aviationarchaeology.com/dbSelectNavy.asp): Searchable U.S. Navy aviation accident reports and loss lists
- [Select Vietnam Database](https://aviationarchaeology.com/dbSelectVietnam.asp): Searchable Vietnam War era USAF aircraft losses 1962-1973

## Core Services & Organization

- [AAIR Homepage](https://aviationarchaeology.com): AAIR root domain homepage with organization overview and mission
- [AAIR Services](https://aviationarchaeology.com/services.asp): AAIR's crash site surveys, recovery services, and historic preservation
- [Aviation Archaeology Course](https://aviationarchaeology.com/course.asp): AAIR weekend course in crash site documentation and fieldwork
- [Books for Sale](https://aviationarchaeology.com/books.asp): AAIR catalog of aviation archaeology and crash history books

## Technical Reference Materials

- [Search for Aircraft Prefixes](https://aviationarchaeology.com/prefixes_search.asp): Searchable database of aircraft part number prefixes by manufacturer
- [Aircraft Prefixes by Manufacturer](https://aviationarchaeology.com/prefixes_manf.asp): Aircraft part number prefix reference organized by manufacturer
- [Aircraft Prefixes by Aircraft Type](https://aviationarchaeology.com/prefixes_type.asp): Aircraft part number prefix reference organized by aircraft type
- [Abbreviations, Acronyms and Codes](https://aviationarchaeology.com/AbbrevAcronymsCodes.asp): Reference guide for aviation military abbreviations and crash codes
- [Inspection Stamps](https://aviationarchaeology.com/stamps.asp): Reference guide for aircraft manufacturer inspection stamps

## Support & Resources

- [How to Order Reports](https://aviationarchaeology.com/orderinfo.asp): Instructions for ordering aircraft accident reports and payment
- [Contact List](https://aviationarchaeology.com/contactlist.asp): Directory of aviation archaeology community members and contacts
- [External Links](https://aviationarchaeology.com/links.asp): Directory of external aviation archaeology organizations and resources

## Optional

- [YAP Expedition - 2006](https://aviationarchaeology.com/listPages/tour_yap/asp/toursyap00.asp): AAIR expedition report from Yap Island WWII aircraft survey
- [AAIR Expedition Vehicles](https://aviationarchaeology.com/vehicles.asp): Documentation of AAIR's modified 4x4 expedition vehicles
